title: Enterprise onboarding, escalation, integration and QBR playbook
author: Sofia Martinez
content:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's standard operating procedures for enterprise customer onboarding, technical integration, escalation handling, known issues and workarounds, and quarterly business reviews (QBRs). It is intended for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support Engineers, and on-call site reliability engineers who participate in customer engagements.

Scope:
- New enterprise customers (Dedicated or Private deployments) from contract signature through first 90 days of production traffic.
- Integration touchpoints with Engineering (runtime, infra), Security, and Product for escalations and feature requests.
- Regular health checks and QBR preparations for ongoing accounts.

Owner and SLAs:
- Owner: Customer Success (onboarding lead) with Solutions Engineering for technical integration.
- Time-to-first-response: 4 business hours for P1 escalations during business hours; follow incident oncall policy for after-hours escalation.
- Onboarding milestone targets: API connectivity & test generation within 5 business days of kickoff; first production traffic within 30 days.

1) Enterprise Onboarding checklist (pre-kickoff to go-live)

Pre-Kickoff (contract signed):
- Assign CSM and SE and schedule kickoff within 3 business days.
- Create internal onboarding workspace and JIRA project; add customer contacts and technical stakeholders.
- Share README and integration checklist with customer.

Kickoff (Day 0):
1. Introductions and roles (CSM, SE, SRE contact, customer technical lead).
2. Review success criteria and KPIs (latency targets, throughput, cost target, compliance needs).
3. Outline timeline and milestones.

Technical Integration (Days 1-14):
- Networking: exchange IP allowlists, VPC peering details (if Private), and TLS cert expectations.
- Auth: confirm API key rotation policy, KMS/HSM integration requirements (if any), and test credentials.
- Model selection & configs: recommended model variant, tokenization, and max_seq_len. Document quantization profile if using Dedicated/private GPUs.
- Test plan: smoke tests for generation, embeddings, streaming, and function calls. Provide sample prompts and expected outputs.
- Observability: ensure access to Console dashboards, per-route metrics, and tracing hooks for SE team.

Go-Live (Days 15-30):
- Canary rollout: route 1-5% traffic to production endpoint for 24-48 hours. Monitor latencies, error rates, and cost per token.
- Performance tuning: adjust batching, cache TTL, and autoscale settings based on observed qps/latency.
- Final sign-off checklist: SLA acceptance, security checklist, runbook handoff, and QBR cadence agreed.

2) Escalation playbook (severity classification and process)

Severity levels:
- P1 (Sev-1): Production outage or severe degradation where customers cannot serve traffic or experience >50% error rate.
- P2 (Sev-2): Significant functional impact (e.g., model regressions causing incorrect outputs for core flows) with workarounds available.
- P3 (Sev-3): Non-critical bugs, performance degradation affecting small percentage of requests.

Escalation matrix and responsibilities:
- Customer reports issue to support@redwood.com or Slack SSO channel; ticket automatically created in Zendesk and routed to Tier 1.
- Tier 1 (Support): initial triage and reproducibility check within SLA (4 business hours for P1 during BH).
- Tier 2 (SE/SRE): engaged for root cause analysis; expected engagement within 1 hour for P1.
- Engineering/Oncall: engaged when issue is traced to runtime/kernel/hardware; incident declared and incident commander assigned.

Escalation steps (numbered):
1. Triage: collect request_id, model, config, request payload (sanitized), timestamps, and route logs.
2. Reproduce: attempt to reproduce in test environment; capture minimal repro case.
3. Mitigation: apply temporary mitigation (traffic reroute to fallback model, scale up Dedicated capacity, or apply rate-limiting) while RCA is performed.
4. RCA and fix: track root cause in ticket/incident doc; provide ETA for fix or vendor patch.
5. Post-incident: write postmortem (link to postmortem in related_pages), share customer-facing summary and action items.

Communication templates (use in ticket updates):
- Initial Acknowledgement: "We have received your report and are actively investigating. Current severity: P1. Assigned team: SRE/SE. Next update in 60 minutes."
- Customer update (mitigation): "We have applied a temporary mitigation by routing traffic to fallback model (vX.Y). Please monitor and report any anomalies."

3) Integration guide (common integrations and checklist)

Network & Security checklist:
| Item | Owner | Required by Go-Live |
|------|-------|--------------------|
| API allowlist / egress rules | Customer & SE | Yes |
| VPC peering or Private endpoint | Customer & Infra | Optional (Private customers required) |
| TLS certs & PKI integration | Customer | As-needed |
| KMS/HSM integration | Security/Customer | If required by compliance |

SDK and API checklist:
- Provide SDK example for customer language (Python/JS): sample repo link and quickstart commands.
- Validate API key scopes and rotation procedure.
- Confirm streaming vs non-streaming requirements and any custom function-calling hooks.

Observability & logging:
- Ensure Console access and set role-based permissions.
- Confirm retention windows required for audit logs.
- Configure alerting thresholds (see "Health checks and alerts" below).

4) Known issues and workarounds (frequent problems seen during onboarding)

Issue: Increased tail latency under bursty traffic
- Symptom: 95th/99th percentile latency spikes during short bursts.
- Root cause: small batch sizes and contention on kernel scheduling under mixed-sequence-length workloads.
- Workarounds: increase min-batch-size and enable request coalescing; set autoscale "burst buffers" to allow short-term capacity; use prefix KV caching for repeated prompts.

Issue: Tokenization mismatch leading to unexpected prompt length
- Symptom: model truncates important context; customer sees partial outputs.
- Root cause: client-side tokenizer differs from model tokenizer or unexpected special tokens in prompt templates.
- Workarounds: provide canonical tokenizer library in SDK, add validation in pre-send hook, and include recommended prompt templates in onboarding repo.

Issue: Auth failures after API key rotation
- Symptom: 401 returned after scheduled rotation.
- Root cause: stale cached keys in CI or in intermediary proxies.
- Workarounds: advise using staged key rotation with rollover window, validate keys in test environment before rotating, and provide rotation checklist.

5) Support process & SLAs (ticket lifecycle)

Ticket lifecycle steps:
1. Ingestion: ticket created via Zendesk, email, or Slack; auto-triaged by severity and product area.
2. Triage: Tier 1 assigns reproducibility and initial ownership.
3. Diagnosis: SE or SRE performs root-cause analysis.
4. Mitigation and fix: implement workaround or timeline for code fix/patch.
5. Closure: customer confirms resolution; close ticket and log action items for product/engineering backlog.

SLA table:
- P1: Initial response within 1 hour (BH), continuous updates every 60 minutes until mitigation.
- P2: Initial response within 4 business hours, updates every 4-8 hours.
- P3: Initial response within 1 business day.

Escalation contacts:
- Oncall SRE Slack: #oncall-sre (use PagerDuty for after-hours).
- SE escalation: se-oncall@redwood.com.
- CSM escalation: csm-lead@redwood.com.

6) Health checks and QBR preparation (metrics, cadence, and templates)

Health check cadence:
- Weekly automated health summary email for high-touch accounts (includes traffic, 99p latency, error rate, cost per 1k tokens, cache hit rate).
- Monthly operational review with SE to tune batch/scale settings.
- Quarterly QBR with executive summary, usage trends, ROI metrics, and roadmap items.

Core QBR metrics (suggested):
- Uptime (SLA) % by region
- 99th percentile latency (ms) and median latency (ms)
- Error rate (% of requests returning 5xx or model-side errors)
- Cost per 1k tokens and trend vs previous quarter
- Model quality signal: precision/recall or customer-defined accuracy for test prompt-set
- Support metrics: Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA), Mean time to resolve (MTTR), number of escalations

QBR template (sections):
1. Executive summary and top outcomes.
2. Usage and adoption trends by product area.
3. Reliability & performance: incidents, mitigations, and improvements.
4. Cost & efficiency: unit economics and Optimize recommendations.
5. Roadmap & requests: upcoming features, integration blockers.
6. Action items and owners (with deadlines).

7) Playbook maintenance and ownership
- The Customer Success director is the document owner; SE and SRE maintain technical sections.
- Review cycle: quarterly review and after every Sev-1 incident to incorporate learnings.
- Change process: submit update PR in the onboarding workspace and notify reviewers listed in this doc.

Appendix: useful commands and snippets
- API smoke test (curl):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-2-small","prompt":"Hello world","max_tokens":32}'

- Troubleshooting checklist (quick): request_id, timestamps, model, route, payload, sample output, SDK version, kernel/runtime version (if available).
